Description: Monorepo, toolchains, shared libraries and enforced code rules (interfaces + impls, no wildcard/inline imports, hexagonal layering).
Create the monorepo (contracts, java, go, web, mobile, docs, infra, design) with CLAUDE.md conventions and the service catalogue.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Repository has contracts/, java/, go/, web/, mobile/, docs/, infra/, design/ directories
- CLAUDE.md documents toolchain versions, layering and import rules
- infra/local/PORTS.md lists every service, runtime, port and data store
- Design handoff (prototypes + chat transcripts) is stored under design/

Summary: Maven reactor and platform parent POM
Description: Spring Boot 4.1.x / Java 25 parent with dependency management, compiler, enforcer, Failsafe, JaCoCo and Jib.
Acceptance Criteria:
- ./mvnw verify builds every Java module from java/
- Java 25 and Maven 3.9 are enforced
- Integration tests (*IT) run in the verify phase via Failsafe
- Spring Boot version is a single property that can be bumped to 4.1.4

Summary: Checkstyle gate: no wildcard or inline imports
Description: Checkstyle rules that fail the build on star imports, inline fully-qualified names, field injection, Lombok and System.out.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A file with import java.util.* fails the build
- A file using java.util.List inline in code fails the build
- @Autowired on a field fails the build
- Rules run in the validate phase for main and test sources

Description: Reusable ArchUnit rules: layer direction, framework-free domain, package-private Impl classes, use cases as interfaces.
Acceptance Criteria:
- platform-test exposes HexagonalArchitectureRules.verify(classes, basePackage)
- Every Java service has an ArchitectureTest that calls it
- A domain class importing Spring fails the test
- A public *Impl class in application fails the test

Summary: platform-web library (API docs pages, problem details, correlation ids)
Description: Shared web conventions for every Spring service.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Every service serves Swagger UI, /docs (Scalar) and /redoc (Redoc) from its /v3/api-docs
- Domain exceptions map to RFC 9457 problem+json with a stable code
- X-Correlation-Id is accepted, generated if missing, returned and put in the MDC
- Reference pages can be disabled per environment (off in prod)

Description: Outbox written in the business transaction, Kafka relay keyed by aggregate id, inbox de-duplication.
Acceptance Criteria:
- DomainEventPublisher.publish requires an active transaction
- Outbox rows are relayed to at.<aggregate>.events with event-id, event-type and occurred-at headers
- Relay uses SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so several pods can run it
- InboxDeduplicator returns false for a redelivered event id

Description: JWT resource-server defaults, Actor resolution from identity claims and fine-grained permission checks.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Docs, health and metrics endpoints are public; everything else needs a valid JWT
- Actor exposes subject, principal type, org id, roles and permissions
- PermissionChecker.require throws a 403 problem when the permission is missing
- Local profile can disable auth and run as a local super admin

Summary: Go workspace and shared pkg module
Description: go.work with a shared module: config loader, slog logging, HTTP runtime, problems, auth, telemetry, Kafka ports.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Each Go service is its own module and builds with GOWORK=off
- Config loads config/<APP_ENV>.yaml then env overrides; unknown env fails fast
- HTTP runtime serves /healthz, /readyz, /metrics, /openapi.yaml, /docs, /redoc
- Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM within 20s

Description: Shared golangci-lint v2 config enforcing no dot/blank imports, wrapped errors and goimports grouping.
Acceptance Criteria:
- golangci-lint run reports 0 issues on every module
- Dot imports and blank imports outside main fail lint
- Unwrapped errors from interfaces and external packages fail lint

Summary: Container images for Java and Go services
Description: Distroless Go images and layered Spring Boot images, non-root, with Jib as CI alternative.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Go images are built FROM distroless/static:nonroot and are under 60 MB
- Java images use layered jars on eclipse-temurin:25-jre and run as uid 1000
- Images default to APP_ENV/SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod and port 8080

Summary: Backlog CSV with Jira import format
Description: Maintain this backlog as a Jira-importable CSV and mark stories Done as they are completed.
Acceptance Criteria:
- docs/backlog/backlog.csv imports into Jira with epics, parent links, priority, points, labels and status
- tools/backlog/mark.py sets a story status by issue id
- Every completed story is marked Done in the same commit as the work

Description: Spring Authorization Server (OAuth 2.1 / OIDC): one account for customers, sellers, providers, staff and drivers; roles decided server-side; social login, MFA, passkeys and RBAC.

Summary: Spring Authorization Server with OIDC discovery and JWKS
Description: Identity service issues access/ID/refresh tokens for web, mobile and services.
Acceptance Criteria:
- /.well-known/openid-configuration and /oauth2/jwks are served
- Authorization Code + PKCE works for the storefront and mobile clients
- Client Credentials works for service-to-service calls
- Access tokens live 5 minutes and carry pt, org, roles and perms claims

Summary: Unified sign-up for customers, sellers and providers
Description: Same form for every account: first name, last name, email, mobile with country code, password, confirm, terms; role decided server-side.
Acceptance Criteria:
- First/last name accept letters, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and accents
- Phone is validated per country and stored in E.164
- Password needs 12+ chars, upper, lower, digit and must not contain the name or email
- Seller/provider entry points add the role server-side; the form never asks for a role
- Duplicate email returns a clear error

Description: Accounts created with email/password verify their email before continuing.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A 6-digit code is emailed and expires after 10 minutes
- Resend is rate limited to 1 per 30 seconds and 5 per hour
- 'Use a different email' restarts sign-up
- Social sign-ups skip the code because the provider verified the email

Summary: Social login via OIDC (Google first, Apple and Facebook configurable)
Description: Federated login through the providers' real OAuth flows; providers appear only when enabled by the platform.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Google sign-in uses the provider's consent page, never a form we fill
- Accounts are created from verified claims (name, email)
- Only providers enabled in Developers › Identity providers appear in the UI
- Official brand logos are used on buttons

Description: Passkey registration and sign-in; 'Sign in with a passkey' only on the sign-in screen.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Users can register, list and remove passkeys in Login & security
- Passkey sign-in works on Chrome, Safari and Firefox
- Create-account screen does not offer passkey sign-in
- Mobile app supports Face ID / fingerprint through platform passkeys

Description: Second factor at sign-in with trusted-browser option; mandatory phishing-resistant MFA for staff.
Acceptance Criteria:
- TOTP enrolment shows QR + recovery codes
- SMS codes respect consent and quiet hours do not apply to OTP
- 'Trust this browser' skips MFA for 30 days
- Staff accounts cannot disable MFA

Description: Users land where their role belongs: shop, Seller Center, Provider Hub, staff console or driver app.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Customers stay in the shop
- Approved sellers/providers land on their dashboard; pending ones on onboarding
- @afrotransact.com staff land in the staff console
- A customer who starts selling gets the seller role on the same account, no second sign-up

Summary: Permission model: permissions, roles, direct grants
Description: Permissions are abilities, roles bundle them, users can hold several roles plus direct grants.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Effective permissions = union of role permissions and direct grants
- Driver app requires delivery:operate; admins can be granted it directly
- Removing a permission revokes it on the next token refresh (≤5 min)
- Every change is written to the audit log

Summary: Access control administration (module matrix, capabilities, people, change log)
Description: Developers and Super Admins manage access in the staff console; Product Owner and Auditor can view.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Module access matrix cycles none → view → edit → approve → full
- Capabilities tab maps roles to permissions
- People tab toggles roles, direct grants and enable/disable
- Change log lists who changed what and when

Summary: Login & security page (password, linked accounts, passkeys, sessions, recovery codes)
Description: Self-service security settings for every account.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Change password requires the current password
- Link/unlink Google, Apple, Facebook (cannot unlink the last sign-in method)
- Active sessions listed with 'sign out other devices'
- Recovery codes can be regenerated

Description: Relationship checks seller_org → store → listing so members only touch their org's data.
Acceptance Criteria:
- OpenFGA model covers org membership, store ownership and listing ownership
- Catalog/orders services check org relationships for non-staff actors
- A catalog member cannot access payouts

Description: One product page per item (ATIN/GTIN), category-specific schemas, variants and category requests.

Summary: Catalog service skeleton with hexagonal layout and docs
Description: Spring Boot catalog service with Flyway, outbox, security and API reference pages.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Service starts on 8101 with local profile against docker compose Postgres
- Swagger UI, /docs and /redoc render the API
- ArchitectureTest passes
- Health, readiness and Prometheus endpoints respond

Summary: Category tree and product-type schemas seeded from design
Description: Department › category › product type tree with required details, variation themes and identifier rule per type.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Seven departments from the design are seeded (Fashion, Groceries, Beauty, Books, Home & Art, Health, Event & party)
- Each product type defines attributes (with options), variation themes and GTIN/ISBN rule
- GET /v1/categories and /v1/product-types are public
- Seed is generated by tools/seed/catalog_taxonomy.py

Description: Product builder submission: category, images, details, variations, SKUs, barcodes and prices validated on the server.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Owner (seller org or AfroTransact Retail) is derived from the token; there is no 'sold by' field
- Title 10–200 chars; every required attribute filled with an allowed value
- 1–10 JPG/PNG/WebP images ≤ 8 MB; main image ≥ 1000×1000 px
- Variant SKUs unique per org; prices > 0; GTIN check digit valid or exemption; ISBN-13 required for books
- All failing fields are returned at once as fieldErrors

Summary: ATIN issuance for products and variants
Description: AfroTransact identifiers (ASIN equivalent) issued from a database sequence.
Acceptance Criteria:
- ATINs match AT + 8 base-36 characters
- Each product and each variant gets its own ATIN
- ATINs are unique across pods and not sequentially guessable

Summary: GTIN check and shared product pages
Description: Validate barcodes while typing and steer sellers to an existing page instead of duplicating.
Acceptance Criteria:
- GET /v1/identifiers/gtin/{code} returns valid flag, suggested correction and existing ATIN
- Creating a product whose GTIN already exists returns 409 with the existing ATIN
- GTIN-8/12/13/14 supported; ISBN-13 enforced for books

Summary: Category requests and building products against them
Description: Sellers request a missing category and can build products immediately; they publish after approval.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Request needs parent path, name, example product and details (3+ chars each) and gets a REQ-###### reference
- Products built against a request are PENDING_CATEGORY_APPROVAL
- Approval creates the product-type leaf and moves waiting products to IN_REVIEW
- Rejection rejects waiting products with the note

Description: Staff with catalog:moderate review submitted products; owners pause/resume live listings.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Only IN_REVIEW products can be approved
- Reject requires a note
- Owners can pause and resume only their own live products
- Each transition publishes a catalog.product.* event via the outbox

Summary: Image upload via UploadThing with moderation checks
Description: Signed uploads, size/dimension checks and background moderation (no watermarks, white background for main).
Acceptance Criteria:
- media service issues UploadThing presigned uploads
- Uploaded image metadata (url, width, height, bytes, type) is returned to the builder
- Images failing moderation are flagged on the product

Summary: Barcode lookup prefill (GS1 / Open Food Facts)
Description: When a seller types a GTIN, prefill name, images and description from product-data providers.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Lookup tries GS1 US Data Hub then Open Food Facts for groceries
- Prefilled fields are editable and marked as imported
- No match falls back to manual entry

Summary: Barcode label generation (GS1-128, Code 128, EAN-13, ZPL)
Description: Generate retail, case, pallet, shelf and AfroTransact unit labels.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Unit labels for platform stock without vendor GTIN use the ATF prefix
- Case labels encode AI 01/10/11/17
- Labels render as PDF and ZPL for printers

Description: Elasticsearch read model with typo tolerance, diaspora synonyms, facets, geo and semantic retrieval.

Summary: Product index mapping with diaspora synonyms
Description: products-<market>-v<N> behind an alias with analyzers, synonyms, search-as-you-type and dense_vector.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Index is created with the shared mapping and aliased to products-<market>
- Synonyms cover gari/garri, zobo/bissap/hibiscus, egusi/melon seed and more
- Mapping version bump allows zero-downtime reindex

Summary: Search API with filters, facets and sorts
Description: GET /v1/search used by the results page, apps and Lola.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Every typed word must match; partial words match
- Typos tolerated: one edit for 3–5 letters, two for 6+
- Filters: department, community, fulfilment, seller kind, rating, price, delivery days, in stock, distance
- Facets returned for department, community, fulfilment, seller kind, rating, price and delivery
- Sorts: relevance, price asc/desc, rating, newest

Description: GET /v1/suggest returns completed phrases (first scoped to a department) and up to five products.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Suggestions appear from the first character
- First phrase includes its department, e.g. 'jollof seasoning in Groceries'
- Products show price, stock and how they ship
- Responses are cacheable for 30 seconds

Summary: Semantic (hybrid) retrieval via AI gateway embeddings
Description: Natural-language queries blend kNN with lexical relevance and degrade gracefully.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Queries of 3+ words request an embedding with a 150 ms budget
- If the embedder fails or times out, lexical results are returned
- Response reports whether semantic retrieval was used

Description: Indexer consumes catalog, offers and inventory events and upserts product documents idempotently by version.
Acceptance Criteria:
- catalog.product.approved creates/updates a document
- inventory.availability.changed updates available_qty and in_stock
- Out-of-order events with an older version are ignored
- Bulk indexing with retries and a dead-letter topic

Description: Product cards and search hits show 'Only N left' at 5 units or fewer.
Acceptance Criteria:
- lowStock is true when 1–5 units are available
- Out-of-stock items show 'Currently unavailable'

Description: Click-through and zero-result logging, ranking boosts for buy-box price, delivery promise and seller health.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Zero-result queries are logged for synonym curation
- Ranking boosts in-stock and Fulfilled-by-AfroTransact items
- A relevance test set runs in CI

Description: Seller offers on shared product pages, price rules, coupons and buy-box selection.

Summary: Offers service: create offer on existing product
Description: Sellers attach price, stock and condition to an existing ATIN instead of duplicating the page.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Offer created from catalog.product.created for the creating seller
- Other sellers can add an offer by ATIN or GTIN
- Offer price, handling time and fulfilment type are stored

Description: Pick the winning offer by landed price, delivery promise, seller health and stock; 1P competes under the same rules.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Winner recomputed on price/stock/health change
- Ineligible offers (no stock, restricted seller) never win
- Selection rules are audited and documented

Description: Platform- or seller-funded coupons with scope, minimum spend, limits and dates.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Coupon types: percent, fixed, free shipping
- Usage limits per coupon and per customer are enforced
- Funding source (AfroTransact or seller) is recorded for settlement

Description: Product page lists other offers for the same item with price, delivery and seller rating.
Acceptance Criteria:
- All eligible offers listed with landed price
- Customers can add a non-buy-box offer to cart

Description: Amazon-style cart split per seller, stock-capped quantities, and a clean three-step checkout saga.
Carts with price snapshots, save for later and merge on login.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Quantities can never exceed sellable stock
- Lines that lose stock are flagged and excluded from checkout
- Guest cart merges into the account cart on sign-in
- Save for later moves lines out of the active cart

Description: 'Add to cart' becomes a − / + stepper; out-of-stock shows 'Currently unavailable' with back-in-stock alert.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Stepper never exceeds available stock
- Out-of-stock items cannot be added
- 'Email me when available' subscribes the user

Description: Validate cart → reserve inventory → PaymentIntent (manual capture) → order + shipments → confirm.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Each step has a compensation (release reservation, cancel intent, void order)
- Idempotency-Key on placeOrder returns the same order on retry
- A failed payment releases reservations within 1 minute
- Cart is cleared after a successful order

Summary: Three-step checkout UI (address, payment, items & delivery)
Description: Each step folds to a summary with Change; order summary stays on the right.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Saved addresses and payment methods load by default
- Add address opens a dialog with address autocomplete
- Add payment method supports card and US bank (ACH) via Stripe Elements
- Apple Pay, Google Pay and Link quick-pay buttons
- No 'use my current location' in checkout

Description: Carrier shipping, AfroTransact Delivery or pickup chosen per package with dates.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Carrier options come from carrier-gateway rate shopping
- AfroTransact Delivery offered only in served zones from nearby origins
- Pickup locations show address, hours and ready time
- Delivery instructions and preference captured; handover code required for perishables or hand delivery

Description: Delivery dates per ZIP from FC cutoffs, carrier SLAs and seller handling time.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Promise shown on cards, PDP, cart and checkout
- The promise is stored on the order and measured against actual delivery

Description: Entering a ZIP in a deactivated state blocks delivery and checkout there.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Deliver-to ZIP in a disabled state shows a clear message
- Checkout cannot proceed with an address in a disabled state

Description: Stripe Connect separate charges and transfers, configurable commission, double-entry ledger and payouts on request.
Create, confirm (3-D Secure), capture per shipment and refund through Stripe.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Manual capture per shipment on carrier acceptance
- 3-D Secure test card triggers authentication
- Declined test card returns a clear error
- Stripe calls reuse the order idempotency key

Description: Signed, de-duplicated, ordered handling of Stripe events.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Signature verified with the endpoint secret
- Duplicate event ids are ignored
- Unknown events are stored and acknowledged

Description: Immutable journal for charges, commission, seller payables, fees, tax, refunds and chargebacks.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Every journal balances (debits = credits)
- Ledger runs at SERIALIZABLE isolation
- Daily reconciliation against Stripe balance transactions alerts on drift

Description: Per-recipient breakdown: items, shipping, tax, commission, FBA fees and pro-rata Stripe fee.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Stripe fee shared pro rata; leftover cents go to AfroTransact
- AfroTransact Retail pays no commission
- Staff can view the split on any order

Description: Commission % per category with seller overrides, card fee and FBA fee, versioned with effective dates.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Only Super Admin and Finance can edit
- Changes apply to new orders only
- Worked two-seller example shown in the UI

Summary: Payouts on request with settlement hold
Description: Earnings held 7 days after delivery/completion; sellers request payouts; finance approves.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Balance shows available, on hold (per order with release date) and requested
- Minimum $25, one request per day, owner/finance roles only
- Connected accounts use manual payout schedule
- Finance can approve, hold or release payout requests

Description: Partial refunds reverse matching transfer and commission; chargebacks debit the responsible seller.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Partial refund per line updates the ledger
- Chargeback debits the seller's balance and notifies them

Description: Orders split into shipments per seller with a role-aware status state machine.
One order, one shipment per seller/fulfilment node, each cancellable separately.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Order totals equal the sum of shipments plus tax
- Each shipment can be cancelled before it is packed

Summary: Shipment state machine with actor rules
Description: placed → confirmed → packed → ready → picked_up → in_transit → out_for_delivery → delivered (+ failed, returned, cancelled).
Acceptance Criteria:
- Seller-fulfilled: only the seller confirms, packs and marks ready
- Carriers (webhooks) and AfroTransact Delivery move transit steps
- Platform admins may confirm delivery, record failure, process returns or cancel — never 'packed'
- Fulfilled by AfroTransact: admins and fulfilment ops own every step
- Rules enforced in the service, not the UI

Summary: Your Orders page with creative side panel
Description: Order history with per-shipment tracking, buy again and a useful right-hand panel.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Each shipment shows status timeline and tracking
- Right panel shows recommendations / delivery map / help instead of blank space

Summary: Driver events update order status live
Description: Driver pickup/delivery scans move shipment statuses in the back office immediately.
Acceptance Criteria:
- 'Picked up' and 'Delivered' scans update the shipment within 5 seconds
- Staff console reflects updates without refresh (SSE)

Summary: Inventory: platform & FBA stock, lots and concurrency
Description: Strongly consistent stock positions, reservations, lots (FEFO) and an append-only ledger.
Epic Name: Inventory: platform & FBA stock, lots and concurrency

Description: inventory_position(sku, node, on_hand, reserved, inbound, damaged, version) + ledger.
Acceptance Criteria:
- available = on_hand − reserved is published via events, never computed in clients
- Every movement writes a ledger row with actor and reason
- Nightly job reconciles ledger sums to positions and alerts on drift

Description: Reserve all lines in one transaction with row locks in key order; idempotent per order.
Acceptance Criteria:
- SELECT … FOR UPDATE in key order prevents deadlocks
- All lines reserve or none do
- Retrying with the same order id never double-reserves
- Flash-sale test: N+25 concurrent checkouts for N units ⇒ exactly N succeed

Description: RESERVE (TTL 15 min) → SHIP → RETURN_RESTOCK / RETURN_DAMAGED; adjustments with reasons.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Expired reservations release automatically
- Adjustments can never go below what is reserved
- Returns put stock back or into damaged after inspection

Summary: Lots with expiry and FEFO allocation
Description: Lots per SKU × FC × bin with made/expiry dates; earliest expiry picked first.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Lot unique per (sku, lot_no, fc)
- Picks allocate FEFO
- Expired lots are blocked from sale nightly
- Lots ≤ 30/60 days are flagged for markdown

Summary: Inventory hub in the staff console
Description: Overview, stock & lots, inbound, POs, suppliers, warehouses, labels, accounting and movements tabs gated by RBAC.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Visible only to roles with inventory access
- Lots can be quarantined, released or written off with reasons
- Movement history traceable per lot for recalls

Description: Sellers send stock into AfroTransact FCs with seller-specific unit labels.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Inbound shipment plan with carton labels
- Units labelled per seller so stock never mixes

Description: Nine-step workflow: product master → PO → approval → shipment/ASN → transit & customs → receiving → validation → lots & GL → sale.
Category managers create 1P products with supplier, HTS code, duty, shelf life, storage, reorder point and price.
Acceptance Criteria:
- SKU and GTIN (AfroTransact GS1 prefix, check digit) assigned automatically
- Listing starts as Draft

Description: Supplier records with lead time, on-time %, defect %, certifications and status.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Supplier scorecards update from receipts
- Inactive suppliers cannot receive new POs

Summary: Purchase orders with approval and FX
Description: Draft → Pending approval → Approved → Sent → Confirmed → Received → Closed; FX captured at PO date.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Orders over $10k need Finance approval
- PO PDF + EDI 850 sent to supplier
- Cancel allowed until a shipment is booked

Description: Shipments with lot/made/expiry from supplier packing list; required customs documents per mode.
Acceptance Criteria:
- ASN lines editable until departure, then locked
- Departure blocked while documents are missing
- Customs clearance blocked by holds

Description: Receivers scan GS1-128 case labels, count good/damaged, split batches, put away and record QA.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Lot 4–20 alphanumerics, unique per SKU; made ≤ today; expiry > made and not passed
- Remaining life ≥ max(90 days, 50% shelf life) or quarantined
- Shortages raise a claim; >2% over is blocked

Description: Landed cost per unit (FOB + freight, insurance, fees, duty) and journal entries per step.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Dr 1310 In transit / Cr 2110 GR/IR at title transfer
- Completing GRN posts Dr 1300/1320 and Cr 1310/2120
- COGS posted at lot landed cost on shipment

Description: PO price × received qty vs supplier invoice (±1%) before payment; FX gain/loss posted.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Variances route to the buyer
- Closing the PO releases payment

Description: Direct carrier integrations behind one Carrier port — no aggregator.
rate(), buy_label(), void(), track(), schedule_pickup(), validate_address() behind one interface.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Each carrier is its own adapter implementing the same Go interface
- Rate shopping fans out in parallel with a 1.5 s budget and caches per cart

Description: USPS rates, labels and polled tracking.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Labels stored as PDF/ZPL in object storage
- Tracking polled on schedule and mapped to shipment states

Description: UPS rates, labels and push tracking.
Acceptance Criteria:
- OAuth token cached and refreshed
- Track Alert events verified, de-duplicated and ordered

Description: FedEx rates, labels and push tracking.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Webhook signatures verified
- Negotiated rates per FC account

Description: DHL Express rates, labels and push tracking for international shipping.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Customs data passed for international parcels
- Push tracking mapped to shipment states

Description: Platform pickup points/lockers and seller-configured pickup with address and hours.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Sellers set their pickup address and hours in Seller Center
- Pickup ready notifications sent to customers

Description: Internal delivery from sellers and FCs to customers with an offline-first driver app.

Summary: Driver app sign-in with access check
Description: Email + password + 6-digit code; only users with delivery:operate get in.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Users without delivery:operate see 'No driver access' with who can grant it
- Revoking access signs the driver out without losing unsynced events

Description: 10 checks with critical items, odometer, fuel, cold-box temperature, 4 live photos and signature.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Failing brakes, tyres or lights blocks the route and reports a defect to dispatch
- Cold-box must read 33–40°F when perishables are on board
- Photos come only from the live in-app camera

Description: Scan every package for the route out of the warehouse.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Unknown or already-scanned labels are rejected
- Manual label entry is available and flagged

Description: Scan packages at seller locations and record who handed them over; handle pickup problems.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Not ready (wait/skip), closed, wrong count and damaged flows
- Pickup confirmation needs all expected scans or a reason

Description: Arrive, scan, choose handover method and take a live, GPS-stamped photo within 150 m.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Handed to customer requires the 4-digit code
- Someone else requires name, relationship and signature
- Safe place blocked for perishables
- Photo stamped with time, GPS and route id

Description: Customer unavailable, access issues, damage, refusal, missing package, unsafe — with required evidence.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Customer unavailable needs call, text and 5-minute wait before reattempt/pickup point/return
- Reattempt stops must be resolved before shift end
- Failed packages scanned back in at end of shift

Description: SOS alerts with GPS; every action queued with idempotency keys and sent in order.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Offline actions queue and sync in order when back online
- Header shows Synced / Syncing / Offline
- SOS alerts dispatch immediately

Description: Plan routes per zone, assign drivers and reassign failed stops.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Driver events stream into Delivery dispatch
- Failed stops can be reassigned to another route

Summary: Seller & provider onboarding with two-step review
Description: Account first, then a resumable, entity-aware application reviewed by two different staff members.
Epic Name: Seller & provider onboarding with two-step review

Description: Applicants can save, sign out and resume exactly where they left off.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Draft autosaves after every change
- Save & sign out returns to 'Welcome back' and resumes on sign-in
- No sidebar or back-office navigation while applying

Summary: Country and phone with launch-list for unsupported countries
Description: All countries with flags; non-live countries disable the rest of the step and offer a launch list.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Only the country picker and 'Notify me at launch' work in a non-live country
- Phone uses a flag/country-code picker, formats as you type and validates mobile numbers (libphonenumber)
- No RFC text shown under the phone field

Description: Fields change with business type (sole prop, LLCs, corporation, partnership, nonprofit).
Acceptance Criteria:
- Sole proprietors: name, SSN/ITIN, DOB (18+), address
- Companies: legal name, EIN, state and date of formation, address, formation document
- Nonprofits: IRS determination letter
- SSN/EIN dashes are added automatically

Description: Owners with ≥ 25%, significant control rules and multi-member requirements.

- Tests: delivery-runs domain + ITs (switch independent of the master switch, effective state, region edits with stale-version conflict), BFF tests, staff console unit tests, Playwright mock spec

- Labels with real barcodes: SSCC pallet (GS1-128, AI 00), case GS1-128 (01/17/11/10/30) and unit EAN-13 / AT-FN Code 128, print and PDF

- Cycle counts (/v1/cycle-counts, contract first): snapshot, counted units, reason-coded variances, posted as audited adjustments, never below reserved

- Retail PO flow: create, approve, send PDF and EDI 850, supplier confirmation, linked inbound shipment with documents (MISSING / PENDING / OK / HOLD), receipts defaulting to the ASN batch, invoice three-way match, item ↔ ATIN link, new item and supplier, list on storefront
- Storefront pipeline verified live: retail.item.listing-changed repoints the 1P offer to the retail SKU; the buy box quantity reaches the PDP (Fulfilled by AfroTransact) and search (offers.buybox.changed carries the winner's quantity; the indexer applies it per variant)
- Delivery dispatch as designed: routes with the route builder, waiting shipments, seller pickups, SOS alerts (acknowledge), vehicle defects (resolve, unblocking the route), driver events
- Seller Center Send to AfroTransact: FBA inbound create, labels, tracking, lots and expiry, scoped to the active organisation by the BFF
- Tests: barcode, form validation and FEFO unit tests; inventory CycleCountIT; offers RetailListingOfferIT; indexer projector and Elasticsearch tests; BFF hub, FBA and dispatch tests; Playwright mock specs (inbound → receive → lot in stock; cycle count variance → adjustment)
- Docs portal page Inventory: from purchase order to the storefront

Summary: Checkout pays with Stripe Elements: inline Payment Element (deferred intent), Express Checkout, token Appearance
Description:
As a shopper I pay in checkout with Stripe's own Payment Element (cards, Link, Cash App Pay, Affirm and whatever the Stripe account enables) and Express Checkout (Apple Pay, Google Pay, Link), styled like the rest of AfroTransact, and can keep a new method for next time.

Stripe's recommended deferred-intent integration: the Elements are created from the cart (mode payment, amount, currency, captureMethod manual to match the order PaymentIntent, setupFutureUsage off_session when saving, the pre-order windows' paymentMethodTypes when they restrict methods) before any PaymentIntent exists. Place order: elements.submit() → POST /v1/checkout/orders {newPaymentMethod, savePaymentMethod} (BFF → orders → payments saveForOffSession) → stripe.confirmPayment({elements, clientSecret, redirect: if_required, return_url /checkout/complete}). Saved methods stay as a choice above it (confirm with the PaymentMethod id, unchanged). The publishable key only comes from STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY on gateway-bff; without it (local only) the storefront shows a labelled stand-in form.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Payment step: Express Checkout Element at the top, saved methods, then "Use a new payment method" with the Payment Element inline (tabs; wallets only in Express Checkout) and "Save for future purchases"; no modal in checkout
- Elements created in deferred mode with the cart total and currency, manual capture; elements.update({amount}) when delivery choices change; setupFutureUsage follows the save checkbox; pre-order restrictions mirror orders' PreorderPayments
- Place order runs submit → order + PaymentIntent → confirmPayment; Stripe errors (submit, decline, authentication) are shown next to the Payment Element and reopen the payment step; no order is created when submit fails
- Redirect methods and 3-D Secure redirects return to /checkout/complete, which confirms through the BFF (orders reads the intent from payments, refreshed from Stripe), polls and opens the placed order; a failed redirect goes back to checkout
- Appearance API variables and rules read at runtime from the design tokens (gold primary, Figtree, radius, colours, selected tab as designed); Your Payments and booking deposits use the same Payment Element / Appearance on a SetupIntent
- PlaceOrderRequest gains newPaymentMethod / savePaymentMethod (gateway-bff contract, BFF validation: exactly one of saved method, wallet, new method); orders CheckoutRequest.savePaymentMethod → payments saveForOffSession (setup_future_usage=off_session)
- Keys: STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (gateway-bff), STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (payments); gateway-bff refuses to start without pk_test_ in dev/uat or pk_live_ in prod, so the stand-in is local-only; check_env_config.py checks Stripe keys are env/secret-store only; docs/engineering/local-development.md explains Stripe test keys and stripe listen
- Tests: storefront unit tests with a fake window.Stripe (deferred options, amount updates, submit → order → confirm order, errors, 3DS return, saved-method path, Express Checkout wiring, Appearance from tokens), Playwright mock-mode specs (stand-in, 3DS stand-in return, fake Stripe inline element and redirect return), BFF config + checkout tests, orders CheckoutIT, payments stripe-mock contract IT

Summary: My account and sign-in & security: proper authenticator QR enrolment everywhere, back-office My account (profile, security, alerts, preferences) separate from the customer account
Description:

- Seller Center and staff console My account at /account, /account/security, /account/notifications, /account/preferences; the UserMenu stays in-app and Open the storefront is an external link
- Profile: work email read-only, job title, phone; Seller Center organisations with switch and Leave (non-owners; identity POST /v1/me/orgs/{orgId}/leave, owners 409); staff roles read-only
- Notifications (back office): role-specific alert topics per channel (email, SMS) with locked compliance/claims/escalation email, personal quiet hours holding SMS and push (notifications service alert preferences, consent checker by template topic)
- Preferences: language, time zone, date order, number style, default table density; applied to every formatter and data table
- Storefront: Your Account hub redesigned to the Shop design (8 areas + Ask Lola), Login & security, Your profile, Notifications & privacy (marketing consent next to Your Privacy Choices, SMS terms, privacy notice)
- Endpoints: identity /v1/me/preferences, /v1/me/work-profile, /v1/me/trusted-browsers, /v1/me/sign-in-activity, /v1/me/orgs/{orgId}/leave; gateway-bff /v1/account/profile, /preferences, /alerts, /sign-in-activity, /trusted-browsers, PATCH /passkeys/{id}, /orgs/{orgId}/leave
Acceptance Criteria:
- Authenticator QR decodes (jsqr) to exactly the otpauth URI; a code computed from the setup key turns the method on; a wrong code is refused
- A seller and a staff user enrol TOTP live, sign out and sign back in with a TOTP code
- Staff cannot turn two-step off; they can switch methods
- Back-office account menu never leaves the back office (storefront link opens in a new tab)

Summary: One location tree for markets and pre-order areas, with market cities
Description:
Settings → Markets & locations and Pre-orders → Pre-order areas were two different editors: a country table with a "Choose live states" modal, and a region editor opened from country/state dropdowns that replaced a state's city list on save. Both screens now use one location tree (web/apps/staff-console/src/components/locations): country → states → cities, showing only what is live or planned (switched-off places behind "Show switched-off"), each node with its status chip, counts ("Texas · 6 cities · 5 live") and what depends on it (open pre-orders). Everything is edited in place and saved per action: status switches (Live / Planned / Off; On / Off for pre-order areas), "Add a state" and "Add a country" as inline gazetteer pickers (the new state appears at once as planned and opens its city search), "Add cities" as an inline multi-select search that appends to the existing list, "Cover every city in <state>", bulk "Switch selected to …", removal with an Undo toast and a dependency guard (a city an open pre-order sells to can't be removed; switching it off is offered). Edits are optimistic and carry the version they loaded (If-Match): a 412 rolls back, says someone else changed it and reloads.

Markets get cities as a first-class part of the model (content owns markets; delivery-runs keeps owning pre-order coverage; the tree component and the geo place lookups are shared): content V11 adds state status (LIVE = marketplace on, PLANNED, OFF), city coverage (every city vs listed cities), market_city with LIVE / PLANNED / OFF and published copies, row versions on countries and states, and draft endpoints to add a state, change a state, append / switch / remove cities. Eligibility takes an optional city (a city listed Planned or Off is not served; a state that doesn't cover every city serves only cities listed Live); without a city the state decides as before, so checkout (orders) is unchanged. The BFF adds /v1/staff/markets/* (with open pre-orders per state and city from delivery-runs and the removal guard), /v1/staff/places (geo gazetteer for both screens), relays upstream 412 as VERSION_CONFLICT (was 502) and sends geo's city with the deliver-to eligibility check.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Only live and planned countries, states and cities show by default; switched-off ones behind a toggle
- Add a state / country inline from the gazetteer; new states appear immediately as planned
- Add cities inline (multi-select search) appends to the existing list; cover every city of a state
- Status switches, bulk switch and removal with undo happen in place; cities an open pre-order uses can't be removed (switch off offered)
- Per-action saves with optimistic UI and If-Match; 412 rolls back with a clear message and reloads
- Markets cities modelled in content (migration, LIVE / PLANNED / OFF, contract-first API, BFF routes, api-client, mocks); eligibility by city; storefront deliver-to still resolves Houston 77042 and Lubbock 79401
- Pre-order areas use the same tree component
- At 390px the tree stacks with 44px touch targets; arrow-key tree navigation, aria-expanded, labelled switches
- Tests: content MarketCitiesIT + domain tests, BFF markets conformance + deliver-to city test, staff console unit/component tests (filters, append, status, guard, 412, keyboard, both screens), Playwright mock spec staff-console.locations.spec.ts

Summary: Operations demo data and local end-to-end orders: purchase orders, inventory, orders, dispatch, returns and payouts with real flows
Description: A super admin found AfroTransact Retail, Inventory, Orders & shipments and Delivery dispatch empty and could not test anything or see how orders and shipments work. Locally there was no way to create a paid order: there is usually no Stripe key, and with security off every caller was the local super admin, so carts were anonymous guest carts (checkout always saw an empty cart), every customer shared one order history, sellers could not pack their own shipments and the driver had no routes. The make seed `ops` step now builds an operations dataset through the services' APIs, and the local stack can take real orders end to end.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `make seed ARGS="--only ops"` (and `make up` when the data is missing) creates, idempotently: 4 suppliers, 8 retail items linked to catalog ATINs, purchase orders in every state (draft, pending approval, approved, sent, confirmed, partially received, received with a matched and with an exception invoice, closed, cancelled), FBA inbound shipments in every stage with lot/made/expiry dates, short-dated, held, damaged and expiring lots, an open and a posted cycle count, a transfer, 14 orders of customer.houston and customer.lubbock in every shipment state (FBA and seller-fulfilled, multi-package, a Lubbock pre-order), routes for driver@afrotransact.test (in progress, an SOS, a vehicle defect, a seller pickup waiting, a completed returns run), returns, an A-to-z claim and a payout request. A second run creates nothing.
- Payments: without STRIPE_SECRET_KEY the local profile uses a stand-in for Stripe (LocalTestStripeGateway, at.payments.stripe.mode auto|local-test|stripe); LocalTestPaymentsPolicy allows it on local only and payments refuses to start with it on dev, uat and prod (LocalTestPaymentsConfigurationTest). With a key, Stripe test mode as before.
- Locally (security off) a request with a customer, driver or seller/provider member token acts as that person (platform-security LocalActorResolver, go/pkg/auth LocalActor); staff and calls without a token keep the super admin. Tested in Java and Go.
- Fixed on the way: delivery-runs resolved no product category (the catalog's public variant view has only categoryId), so nothing was ever a pre-order; orders read shipFromLocationId at the wrong level of offers' PublicOfferDetail, so AfroTransact Delivery from a seller's store could never be checked out; staff 'Update shipment status' offered a fixed list (no packed, ready, picked up, in transit) and now offers each shipment's nextActions; Seller Center called account health (owner and finance only) on every page for every member.
- Staff Orders & shipments has a 'How it works' tab (mirrors the inventory hub's Workflow tab) linking the new portal guide docs/portal/docs/architecture/orders-and-shipments.md; tax-returns runs in the default local stack (Disputes › Returns).
- Verified on the running stack: every staff module and tab shows data with no failed BFF calls; Seller Center as seller.owner, seller.staff, retail.operator and provider.owner; the customers' order history on the storefront; a PO walked from create to received and an order from packed to delivered in the UIs.

Summary: Start selling / Offer your services: straight into a prefilled application (SSO), or create an account first
Description:
As a shopper who wants to sell (or offer services) I want "Start selling" to take me straight into my seller application, signed in and with what AfroTransact already knows filled in, instead of a bare "Sign in to Seller Central" page; and if I have no account, to create one, confirm my email and land in the application.
Reported: Start selling on the storefront opened Seller Center /onboarding?role=seller with a 'Sign in to Seller Central … Sign in' interstitial although the user was signed in on the storefront.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Storefront /sell and /provide: a signed-in shopper is sent to the BFF hosted sign-in on Seller Center's own origin (SELLER_CENTER_URL) with returnTo=<Seller Center>/onboarding?role=seller|provider; identity's session passes it straight through (no credential page). A guest gets prompt=create&intent=sell|provide.
- Identity: the authorization request's intent (sell|provide, Seller Center requests only) brands the hosted sign-up ('Create your account to start selling' / 'Create your account to offer your services', 'Already have an account? Sign in') and the account it creates gets account.seller_applicant / provider_applicant. After the emailed code (Mailpit locally) the request continues into onboarding signed in; 'Sign in' continues there too.
- BFF: POST /v1/seller/onboarding {kind} (idempotent; 201 started, 200 resumed): adds the applicant role (identity POST /v1/me/roles/{kind}-applicant), starts the seller application with a prefill of name, email, phone (verified or not), the default address-book address and an existing organisation's name; 403 STAFF_CANNOT_APPLY for staff accounts, 409 ALREADY_APPROVED, 409 APPLICATION_EXISTS. PUT /v1/seller/onboarding/business and /business-details autosave the first two steps; OnboardingStatus carries form (answers + prefilled). Until approval the seller session shows the application's DRAFT organisation (onboarding only). GET /v1/auth/login passes intent.
- Seller service: StartApplicationRequest.prefill (givenName, familyName, email, phone, storeName, address) used where the token's claims have nothing; a resumed draft gets known values only in answers still empty; prefilledFields gains business.storeName and businessDetails.address.
- Seller Center: no 'Sign in to Seller Central' interstitial: signed out, every page goes straight to the hosted sign-in and back. /onboarding?role=… starts or resumes the application automatically (approved sellers go to Seller Center home, switching organisation if needed); the onboarding page shows the 'Your business' and 'About you' steps prefilled with 'From your account' tags and the design's 'Using your existing AfroTransact account' banner, then the progress checklist (labels fixed, no duplicate review row).
- Tests: storefront /sell route (signed in vs not); Seller Center entry decision, prefill mapping and shell arrival (start once, approved → home, signed out → hosted sign-in); BFF start/resume/staff/approved/autosave and login intent, contract conformance; seller OnboardingFlowIT prefill + resume fill; identity HostedPagesIT seller sign-up branding and applicant role; live Playwright tests/e2e/live/start-selling.live.spec.ts (customer.houston, a new account via Mailpit, seller.owner).

Summary: No hosted payment links and no double charge: pay-now page with Stripe Elements, end-to-end idempotency
Description: As a customer I want to pay only on AfroTransact's own pages and never be charged twice for any reason (retries, double clicks, lost answers, a second device, late webhooks, staff retries), so that a payment problem never turns into a double charge or a trip to a Stripe-hosted page.
Acceptance Criteria:
- No hosted payment pages: payments has no Checkout Session / Payment Link path (gateway method, PaymentLink, paymentLinkHours / paymentLinkUrl removed from API and contract; V12 keeps old rows as legacy_checkout_session). Late pre-order adds paid by link get an ordinary manual-capture PaymentIntent (<orderId>:create-intent).
- Pay-now link: the SMS opens <storefront>/orders/<number>/pay?token=<HMAC token, expiring, bound to order id + number>; the page confirms the existing PaymentIntent with the Payment Element + Express Checkout (same components and Appearance as checkout, confirmPayment redirect if_required) and refuses invalid (404), expired/voided (410) and paid links (no client secret). Orders: POST /v1/service/pay-links/{n}/lookup|confirm (orders:pay-link); BFF: POST /v1/pay-links/{n}/lookup|confirm (public, rate-limited). Expiry cancels the PaymentIntent. Settings label: "Send a pay-now link by SMS (opens the AfroTransact payment page)". SMS fits one segment.
- Late adds: Idempotency-Key required in BFF and delivery-runs (422; random fallback removed); the console makes one per dialog, reuses it until added and looks the result up after a timeout before retrying; a replay texts the link once; orders refuses a second live late add of the same window + items for the customer within 10 min under another key (409 orders.late-add-duplicate). BFF slowTimeout 20s > delivery-runs' 15s.
- Checkout: one open checkout per customer (partial unique index); another key with the same cart resumes it, another cart supersedes it (intent cancelled, stock released) or is refused (PREVIOUS_CHECKOUT_PAID / CHECKOUT_IN_PROGRESS). Web and mobile keep the key until placed or definitely failed (status checked first), single-flight Place order, Express Checkout ignored while busy; booking deposits keep their key the same way. BFF orders slowTimeout 25s > checkout-response-timeout 20s in every env (check_env_config.py).

Summary: Responsive web: phones and tablets in the storefront, Seller Center, staff console and hosted sign-in pages, measured by a CI audit
Description:
As a shopper, seller, provider or staff member on a phone or tablet I want every web page to fit the screen and stay usable with a finger — no sideways scrolling, no clipped or letter-by-letter text, no navigation pushing the page off screen, nothing covering the main button — so that the web apps work as well on 320–1024px screens as on a desktop.
Measured first: tests/e2e/specs/*.responsive.spec.ts audit every route of the three apps (and tabs, sheets, menus) at 320×568, 360×800, 390×844, 414×896, 768×1024, 834×1194, 1024×768, 1280×800 and 1440×900 against the mock BFF, with tests/e2e/scripts/responsive-report.mjs ranking the findings; the before/after counts are in the PR.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Audit (tests/e2e/support/responsive.ts): page overflow, elements past the viewport, clipped text, fixed layers over controls at the end of the page and over the primary CTA, sticky header over 25% of a phone, cramped table cells (<56px), <main> pushed below 60% of a phone, tap targets <24 (crowded) / <44px at touch widths, fonts <12px, narrow phone fields, images without an aspect box, CLS. Specs fail on critical/major findings; RESPONSIVE_OUT writes JSON + screenshots; RESPONSIVE_WIDTHS narrows the run; tests are tagged @responsive.
- Result: zero page overflow, zero elements past the viewport, zero clipped text, zero cramped cells and no covered CTA on every audited page at every width (storefront, Seller Center + Provider Hub, staff console); identity hosted pages checked at 320–1280 from their templates.
- Storefront: compact two-row phone header (logo, deliver-to, account, cart; full-width search) with a sideways-scrolling department bar; on short phones the first row tucks away while scrolling down (sticky offset, no layout shift); announcement bar and pre-order ribbon shrink to a line on phones. Product grids 2 columns on phones, 3–4 on tablets; hero carousel swipeable; PDP gallery full-bleed with the buy box under the price; cart and checkout single column with the subtotal / Proceed to checkout bar and (once actionable) Place your order stuck to the bottom; search filters in a non-modal side sheet (full width on phones) with Show results; footer link columns become accordions; cookie banner is a compact bottom sheet and the page reserves its height; toasts drop under the header on phones.
- Back offices: @afrotransact/ui BackofficeFrame — phones get a Menu disclosure in the header that expands the navigation inline (no overlay) and closes on navigation; tablets (768–1023px) a collapsible 72px icon rail; desktops the fixed sidebar. Header safe-area padding, compact tag/locale on small phones.
- @afrotransact/data-table: below a 36rem container (phones, narrow sheets) rows become stacked cards (first column as title, checkbox kept, label/value pairs) with a Sort select instead of headers; on tablets columns never shrink below ~96px — the table scrolls sideways with the checkbox and first column pinned. Toolbar wraps (full-width search). .at-table detail tables scroll inside their box on phones.
- Global: fluid 2xl–5xl type (clamp) and notch-safe gutters in a web-only tokens layer (native token set unchanged); on touch screens 12px minimum text and 44px controls; viewport-fit=cover; dvh instead of vh; :hover styles behind @media (hover: hover); touch-action: manipulation on controls; tabs scroll sideways and keep the active tab in view; sheets full width and dialogs inset on phones.
- Identity hosted pages (auth.css, layout/error templates): one column edge to edge at 320–560px with safe-area padding, 44px fields and targets, wrapping buttons, viewport-fit=cover, dvh; tokens.css copy refreshed (DesignTokensSyncTest).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Staff console > Developer > Identity & access, visible only with a new permission identity:admin (super admin by default); every change writes the access log (who, what, before/after) and needs step-up MFA
- Clients: list every registered OAuth client (web BFF, customer-app, driver-app, service accounts) with type, grant types, scopes, redirect and post-logout URIs, PKCE/consent flags and token lifetimes; create, edit and disable clients; rotate a confidential client's secret (shown once, old one valid for a grace period); startup provisioning only creates missing clients and never overwrites edits made here
- Sessions & tokens: search active sessions and refresh tokens by user or client (device, IP, last used); revoke one, all of a user's (sign out everywhere) or all of a client's; revoked refresh tokens stop working immediately
- Signing keys: show the JWKS keys (kid, algorithm, created, active/retiring); rotate: a new key signs new tokens while the old one stays published until the longest access token has expired, then retires
- Token inspector: paste a JWT to see header, claims, scopes, expiry and whether signature and issuer validate (tokens never stored or logged); view the OIDC discovery document and JWKS
- Settings: password policy, MFA requirement per portal, session idle/absolute timeouts and access/refresh token lifetimes stored in the identity database, validated, read at runtime and audited (env/config values stay the defaults)

Summary: Manual credits and adjustments with reason codes

Summary: Payments: withhold plan fees from settlement transfers
Description: Collect seller and provider plan fees from their marketplace earnings before charging their card, configurable per seller (sellers may want plan fees as a separate card expense for their own accounting). Payments accepts a withholding for an invoice, deducts withheld fees from the organisation's next settlement transfers in the ledger and releases a withholding when the invoice is voided or refunded; the seller service withholds while Stripe's renewal invoice is a draft and credits the customer balance so the card pays only the rest. COLLECT_PLAN_FEES_FROM_EARNINGS stays the kill switch (on in local and dev).
Acceptance Criteria:
- Per-organisation setting planFeeCollection: EARNINGS_FIRST ("Pay your plan from your sales": pending earnings first, the card for any remainder) or CARD ("Charge my card"); Seller Center Plan & billing toggle with an explanation, changeable by owner and finance only, applied from the next invoice (the invoice date is shown)
- The onboarding Plan step offers the choice, defaulting to the platform default; the staff console sets the platform default for new sellers (Plans & billing › Settings) and overrides one seller in its billing panel, audited with a reason code
- COLLECT_PLAN_FEES_FROM_EARNINGS is a kill switch: off disables collection everywhere and hides the toggle; on by default in local and dev, documented, checked by check_env_config
- invoice.created (draft renewal of an EARNINGS_FIRST seller): POST /v1/orgs/{orgId}/plan-fee-withholdings (seller-service token, scope payments:plan-fees; Idempotency-Key plan-fee-<invoice>) withholds up to the invoice amount less credits from delivered, untransferred earnings, never from orders under an open dispute: WITHHELD (possibly partial; the card pays the rest) or DECLINED with a reason
- The seller service credits the Stripe customer balance by what was withheld (Idempotency-Key earnings-<invoice>) before the invoice finalises; transient failures are retried (503 to Stripe, job with back-off) and never withhold or credit twice
- Payments records Dr 2000:org / Cr 4600 and reduces the next transfers by it (PLAN_FEE_SETTLED, one "Plan fee (invoice …)" deduction per settlement)
- Voided, deleted or out-of-band refunded invoices release the withholding back to the next transfer (and take the balance credit back)
- Seller Center shows "Paid from your sales: $X · Card: $Y" on each invoice and the plan fee deductions on Payouts
- Contracts: payments.yaml, seller.yaml, gateway-bff-seller.yaml and gateway-bff-staff.yaml (embedded copies identical), clients regenerated; payments domain tests and Testcontainers ITs for payments and seller (Stripe stub: balance transactions and Idempotency-Keys), BFF conformance, component tests, Playwright mock journeys

Summary: Rewards: "less than" rules checked at window end (low-sales relief)
Description: Reward rules can reward a quiet start: "1st month free (the trial) and 2nd month free if the seller sold less than $1,000". A rule compares its metric AT_LEAST (as before) or LESS_THAN, its window can start at approval or at the subscription's start (the trial's first day), and a LESS_THAN rule (or an AT_LEAST rule that asks) is decided once, when its window closes: a scheduled job checks it a configurable lead (default 24 h) before the window or the trial ends, so the free days move trial_end before Stripe creates the first invoice.
Acceptance Criteria:
- reward_rule.comparison AT_LEAST (default, existing rules migrated) or LESS_THAN (strictly under: exactly $1,000 does not qualify for less than $1,000); window_anchor APPROVAL (default) or SUBSCRIPTION_START (subscription.started_at, backfilled from current_period_start); check_at_window_end and check_lead_hours (default 24, 0-168)
- A rule decided at window end needs a window (first N days), no rolling window and a summed metric; events never decide it: the window-end job (every 15 min) and the daily job do, once the check is due (lead before the window closes, or before the renewal when Stripe would invoice first) and until the lead has passed after the window closed
- Sales recorded after the check are not counted (documented); the metric is read from the anchor's day to the check's day
- Idempotent per (rule, seller, window): reward_window_check unique (rule_id, org_id, window_start), written in the grant's transaction (QUALIFIED with the grant, or NOT_QUALIFIED); billing_grant stays unique per (rule, seller)
- The reward uses the existing free-days mechanism: trial_end moved with proration_behavior=none and Idempotency-Key grant-<id>-trial
- Staff rule editor: Comparison and Window starts at fields, the check lead, the rule in plain words ("Sellers on Seller Growth who sell less than $1,000 in the first 30 days of their subscription get 30 free days (checked 24 h before the trial ends)") and Who qualifies now with sellers in their window pending until it is checked, with their sales so far
- Seller Center: no progress bar for a LESS_THAN rule but a neutral note with the check date; once applied, "Low-sales relief applied: your next charge is on <date>"
- Contracts: seller.yaml, gateway-bff-seller.yaml and gateway-bff-staff.yaml (embedded copies identical), clients regenerated; LowSalesReliefTest (boundary, anchoring, timing, idempotency, trial extension), LowSalesReliefIT (Stripe stub), BFF conformance, component tests, Playwright mock journeys; docs/engineering/plans-and-billing.md worked example

Summary: Sign out to the app's own sign-in, and reset a forgotten password

Summary: Seller Center fees source and Provider Hub take-home with connection fee
Description: Sellers see where each rate comes from; providers see what they keep after the connection fee before accepting a booking and on earnings.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Fees page shows the plan, the source per category (Negotiated rate until <date>, Your plan: <plan>, Category rate, Standard rate) and the negotiated rates
- Providers see their connection fees per service category
- Booking requests show You keep $X after the N% connection fee
- Earnings report the connection fee as its own column and total
- Component tests; i18n in every locale

Summary: Staff assign a negotiated (invite-only) plan to a seller directly
Description: Negotiate plan price creates a private invite-only plan and invites the organisation, but seller-service only lets the organisation's owner change its plan. Add a staff plan-change operation (seller:billing.manage, audited, with reason and proration rules) so staff can move the seller onto the negotiated plan.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Seller-service staff endpoint to change an organisation's plan with a reason, audited
- gateway-bff Negotiate plan price can assign the plan in the same step
- Staff console shows the assignment in the seller billing panel
